name: @guardbee/mcp-memory-poisoning-scanner
description: MCP server that scans agent code for memory-poisoning risks — untrusted input written into persistent, cross-session memory (MemGPT-style archival/core memory, or a vector store used as a long-term knowledge base) that later gets recalled and trusted as context
long_description: Scans agent source code for two related risks around persistent memory. Memory write: untrusted input (raw tool/user input, request bodies) written directly into archival/core memory (MemGPT-style) or a vector store used as a long-term knowledge base, without a visible sanitization step — since this memory is recalled across future, unrelated sessions as trusted background knowledge, planting content here is a delayed, stored form of prompt injection. Memory read-back: a memory or vector-store retrieval result fed directly into a system/assistant-role message or a prompt template, meaning anything ever planted in that store now speaks with system-level authority. Ordinary short-lived conversation-buffer memory holding raw chat turns is explicitly out of scope — that's just conversation history, not a vulnerability; this package targets only the persistent, cross-session memory path. No API key required — runs entirely locally, static analysis only.
